source.title_on_document: Agency Configurations in Generative AI Ideation: How Textual and Visual Idea Concretizations Shape Idea Creativity and Ideator Effort

supplement.where: Online appendix at https://doi.org/10.1287/isre.2024.0952 (PDF p. 2, 'Supplemental Material')
supplement.holds: Appendix A (example interaction flows; check that initial idea creativity did not differ across conditions), B (GPT and DALL-E prompts, LLM-judge prompt), C (survey scales), D (descriptives and scale validation, likely arm-level means and SDs), E1 (bootstrapping at low idea maturity), E2 (separate Prolific sample using ChatGPT freely), E3 (alternative operationalizations and models). Per-arm counts, arm means and SDs, and separate novelty and usefulness results are not in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: 276 U.S. Prolific participants were assigned to one of three between-subjects arms in an online ideation task (improve the experience on a crowded train): AI-generated textual concretizations of their idea (gpt-3.5-turbo), AI-generated visual concretizations (DALL-E 3), or a no-AI control told to imagine the idea in use. Participants refined their idea over one or more iterations (428 refinements in total). Each refinement was scored for idea creativity, the mean of an embedding-based novelty score and a GPT-4o usefulness score, and for ideator effort (keystrokes and time).

studies.label: Main online experiment (train ideation, three arms)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Type of AI concretization received after describing an initial idea: textual (GPT), visual (DALL-E 3), or none (control instructed to imagine the idea in a usage context)
assignment.quote: Moreover, although we randomly assigned ideators to experimental groups, ideators' preferences or their prior GenAI experiences might have influenced our results.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 12), Section 6.3 Limitations; design described as 'a three-cell, between-subjects online experiment' at PDF p. 8 (printed p. 7), Section 4.1

arms.name: Textual concretization
arms.description: After describing an initial idea, the ideator received an AI-generated textual usage scenario of the idea (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613) and could refine the idea and iterate with the platform

arms.name: Visual concretization
arms.description: After describing an initial idea, the ideator received a DALL-E 3 image of the idea (GPT turned the idea into a prompt of at most 50 words) and could refine the idea and iterate

arms.name: Control (no concretization)
arms.description: Same iterative refinement process, but instead of a concretization the ideator received instructions to imagine the idea and its outcomes in a usage context; described as the baseline for human-only ideation

participants.exclusions: The paper says 276 participants were 'recruited' and contributed 428 idea refinements; it reports no exclusions and no count at assignment. Regressions use N = 428 refinements (endnote 5), so it is not stated whether every one of the 276 contributes at least one row. Per-arm counts are not given in the PDF.
participants.who: U.S.-based Prolific participants; mean age 41.3, 43.8% female, 77.8% with at least a bachelor's degree, 74.2% working full or part time; paid $2, $4 bonus for the 10 best ideas
participants.quote: We recruited 276 U.S.-based participants through Prolific (mean age = 41.3 years old, 43.8% female, 77.8% with at least a bachelor's degree, and 74.2% working full or part time) who contributed a total of 428 idea refinements.

ai_tool.name_model: gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 (textual concretizations and prompt writing for images); DALL-E 3 (visual concretizations)
ai_tool.how_used: The ideator typed an initial idea; the platform returned one AI-generated textual scenario or image that concretized that idea; the ideator then revised the idea text and could repeat the cycle until satisfied. Participants did not chat freely with the model.

task.description: Open-innovation style challenge: 'What improvements could be made to a crowded train to enhance the experience from boarding to alighting?' Each participant provided one idea and refined it iteratively.

outcomes.name: Idea creativity (mean of novelty and usefulness) of each idea refinement
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Novelty: three-nearest-neighbor embedding distance (all-mpnet-base-v2) among ideas at the same refinement stage, following Just et al. (2024). Usefulness: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as judge, mean of feasibility, elaboration, and inclusivity, each iteration scored three times and averaged (Llama 70B gives r = 0.73). Creativity = average of novelty and usefulness, z-standardized at the iteration level. Validation: 88 Prolific workers rated 158 ideas (ICC 0.6); correlation with the creativity score Pearson r = 0.27 (endnote 3). Novelty and usefulness are not reported separately in the PDF. Robustness to other operationalizations and a bootstrapping analysis are in Online Appendix E1 and E3.

contrasts.reported: Backward-difference contrast 'Textual Concretization' (textual vs visual), OLS with clustered robust SEs, N = 428 refinements: Model (1a) 0.29** (0.11); Model (1b, controls) 0.23* (0.10); Model (1c, with maturity interactions) 0.20* (0.08). Textual Concretization x Idea Maturity 0.24** (0.09). Endnote 6: 0.29 SD; adjusted predictions -0.06 SD (51st percentile) for visual vs 0.23 SD (60th percentile) for textual, 'approximately 18%'. R2 0.03 in Model (1a).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 2 and Section 5; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 13), endnote 6; Figure 4 on PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10)

contrasts.reported: Backward-difference contrast 'Visual Concretization' (visual vs control): Model (1a) 0.13 (0.10); Model (1b) 0.17† (0.10) [† p <= 0.10]; Model (1c) 0.14 (0.10). Visual Concretization x Idea Maturity 0.04 (0.13). Text: 'we detected a slight improvement for visual concretizations relative to the control group (beta = 0.17, p <= 0.1)'. Online Appendix E1: visual concretizations significantly increased creativity for idea maturity more than one SD below the mean (statistics not in this PDF).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10), Section 5 text

contrasts.reported: 'Textual concretizations produced a 30% increase in idea creativity compared with the control condition, which is a statistically significant difference.' No coefficient, SE, or p-value printed for this contrast (backward-difference coding reports only textual vs visual and visual vs control).

outcomes.name: Ideator effort (keystrokes and time spent, log)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean of scaled number of keystrokes (including deletions and edits) and time between first and last keystroke, log-transformed (skewness 2.24, kurtosis 12.02). A process measure of effort, not a creativity score; listed so the comparison can see it was considered.

contrasts.reported: Model (2a) 0.24** (0.08); Model (2b) 0.17** (0.06); Model (2c) 0.16*** (0.04); Textual x Maturity 0.23** (0.08). Text: textual required 30% more effort than visual.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10), Section 5

contrasts.reported: Model (2a) -0.26*** (0.07); Model (2b) -0.16*** (0.05); Model (2c) -0.16*** (0.04). Text: visual reduced effort by 24% relative to control; no difference between textual and control.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table 2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10), Section 5

company_involvement.description: Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (Grant 248164); no company involvement stated. Models used are OpenAI products accessed through the authors' platform.

eligibility.reason: S1 randomly assigned individuals to AI textual concretizations, AI visual concretizations, or a no-AI control (random assignment stated in Section 6.3, PDF p. 13; three-cell between-subjects design in Section 4.1, PDF p. 8). 276 participants recruited, well above 50, though per-arm counts and any exclusions are not stated. Creativity is scored on each idea refinement by an automated score (embedding novelty plus GPT-4o usefulness). Caveat: the analysis is at the refinement level (N = 428) with clustered robust SEs whose cluster level is not named explicitly; the textual-vs-control contrast has no printed coefficient.

one_line_finding: In a three-arm Prolific experiment (276 people, 428 idea refinements), AI textual concretizations raised automated idea creativity relative to AI visual concretizations by 0.29 SD (SE 0.11, Table 2 Model 1a, PDF p. 10), while visual concretizations versus a no-AI control were not clearly different (0.13, SE 0.10); the paper states textual beat control by 30% without printing the estimate.
open_questions: Per-arm counts and whether all 276 participants appear in the N = 428 refinement-level regressions are not in the PDF; Online Appendix D may have them.
Clustered robust standard errors: the cluster variable is not named explicitly (text says they capture ideator-level differences and idea-level autocorrelation).

Whether the 428 refinement-level rows include the initial (pre-concretization) ideas is not fully explicit; Section 5 says effects are measured 'beyond the initially submitted ideas' and endnote 5 says N counts idea refinements, so the outcome is coded as produced with AI available.
Textual vs control estimate is described only as a 30% statistically significant increase; the coefficient is not printed.
Separate novelty and usefulness results, if any, are only in the online appendix.
notes: Backward-difference coding: 'Textual Concretization' = textual vs visual; 'Visual Concretization' = visual vs control (PDF p. 9, Section 4.3.1). Controls in Models 1b/2b: trait creativity, perceived mental outcome simulation, perceived ease of use, iterations, age; some are post-treatment survey measures. Initial idea creativity did not differ across conditions (PDF p. 10, Section 5; details in Online Appendix A). The search record's 'RCT?' flag is resolved: randomization is stated, but only in the limitations section. Ideator effort (S1-O2) is not a creativity outcome and is recorded with question 'none'. S1 outcomes are coded as produced with AI available because the regressions use idea refinements written after receiving a concretization (endnote 5); the control arm had no AI throughout.
